section_summary: This section concludes Japan’s 1938 report to the League of Nations on opium and dangerous drugs, covering the Kwantung Leased Territory, the South Seas Mandate, and special prepared-opium reports for Taiwan and Kwantung. Later documents concern State and Treasury Department circulation of the report, customs investigations involving Richard Soriano and Japanese ships, and 1944 correspondence with League of Nations drug-control officials. The section ends with a detailed League analysis of Japanese narcotics legislation, production, trade, addiction, and illicit trafficking, followed by a declassification request for the covering despatch.

subfiles.title: Annual report on traffic in opium and other dangerous drugs for 1938: concluding sections and prepared-opium reports
subfiles.about: Reports on narcotics regulation, addiction, production, smuggling, enforcement, and prepared-opium monopolies in Japanese-administered territories during 1938.
subfiles.summary: The report describes amendments that placed prepared-opium manufacture in the Kwantung Leased Territory under government monopoly and imposed detailed controls on smokers, retailers, medical vendors, dross, and smoking utensils. It supplies statistics on addiction treatment, illicit trafficking, seizures, manufacture, consumption, shops, revenue, and enforcement in Kwantung, while reporting virtually no drug problem in the South Seas Mandate. Special reports for Taiwan and Kwantung describe compulsory treatment, police surveillance, shrinking licensed-smoker populations, government opium sales, and the increasing substitution of morphine for scarce prepared opium.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Japan’s annual narcotics report to the Federal Security Agency
subfiles.to: Administrator of the Federal Security Agency
subfiles.about: Forwards a copy of Japan’s annual report on opium and dangerous drugs for the records of the Public Health Service.
subfiles.summary: State sends the Federal Security Agency Japan's annual narcotics report under the 1931 Convention, for the Public Health Service.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Japan’s 1938 narcotics report to the Treasury Department
subfiles.about: Sends Japan’s 1938 annual narcotics report and additional copies for federal narcotics and customs offices.
subfiles.summary: State forwards Japan's 1938 report on opium and dangerous drugs to Treasury, with copies for the Commissioner of Narcotics and Customs Agency Service.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of Customs report concerning Richard Soriano
subfiles.about: Transmits three copies of a Los Angeles Customs report about Richard Soriano and suspected narcotics associations.
subfiles.summary: Treasury forwards a June 3, 1941 Los Angeles Customs report on Richard Soriano, an associate of suspected narcotics traffickers.

subfiles.title: Customs report on Richard Soriano and jewelry aboard the Tatsuta Maru
subfiles.to: Unnamed customs official in San Francisco
subfiles.about: Reports the inspection of Richard Soriano and his wife upon their arrival at Los Angeles aboard the Japanese ship Tatsuta Maru.
subfiles.summary: Customs examined jewelry declared by Richard Soriano and his wife aboard the Tatsuta Maru; they said it was personal, and further investigation found no undeclared jewelry.

subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to an aide-mémoire on Customs' search of the Japanese Nisshin Maru at Port Costa over suspected narcotics from a Costa Rican port.

subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a memorandum on a Japanese Embassy counselor's call about the Customs search of the Nisshin Maru.

subfiles.about: Points to a telegram explaining the mailing and replacement of two missing narcotics-related despatches.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram 47: despatches 119 and 122 were in a registered item sent to Baghdad October 3, and copies are being forwarded.

subfiles.title: Instruction to forward Japanese narcotics-law translations to Bertil A. Renborg
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, London
subfiles.about: Requests delivery to Bertil A. Renborg of George A. Morlock’s letter and translations of Japanese narcotics laws.
subfiles.summary: Instruction to London to forward Morlock's letter and English translations of Japanese narcotics laws to Bertil Renborg of the League Secretariat.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting Japanese opium and narcotics legislation
subfiles.about: Sends the available translations of Japanese opium and narcotics legislation requested by Renborg.
subfiles.summary: Morlock sends Renborg the revised Opium Law, the August 1941 Ordinance Controlling Narcotics in China and Foreign Affairs Ministry regulations, the only relevant laws the Department holds.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of conversation concerning Japanese narcotics regulations
subfiles.about: Records Leon Steinig’s communication of Renborg’s urgent request for Japanese drug-control legislation.
subfiles.summary: Steinig tells Morlock that Renborg urgently requested copies of the amended 1919 regulations and Japanese legislation since 1938.

subfiles.title: Despatch transmitting a League of Nations note on drug control in Japan
subfiles.from: John N. Allison, for the Ambassador, United States Embassy, London
subfiles.about: Forwards a League of Nations analytical note on Japan’s drug situation and narcotics-control system.
subfiles.summary: London Embassy sends a League note on drug control in Japan and Renborg's covering letter for Morlock.

subfiles.title: Covering letter for note on the Japanese drug situation
subfiles.about: Encloses the League’s note on Japan and discusses possible publication of similar Far Eastern studies.
subfiles.summary: Renborg sends Morlock the League note on Japan's drug situation; the League is considering publishing notes on Far Eastern countries.

subfiles.title: The Drug Situation and the Control of Narcotic Drugs in Japan
subfiles.from: Drug Control Service, Secretariat of the League of Nations
subfiles.about: Analyzes Japan’s international obligations, narcotics laws, control system, production, manufacture, trade, addiction, penalties, and illicit trafficking.
subfiles.summary: The note synthesizes Japanese legislation and reports through 1938, together with statistical returns supplied to the Permanent Central Opium Board. It reviews treaty ratifications, the differing legal treatment of opium and other narcotics, government control of raw opium and coca cultivation, licensed manufacture, estimates, consumption, stocks, imports, exports, wholesale and retail trade, and physician reporting of addicts. It emphasizes the relatively weak penalties under administrative narcotics ordinances compared with the Opium Law and Penal Code. The final section contrasts sparse Japanese reporting with evidence presented by the United States, Canada, and China of extensive international illicit traffic involving Japanese sources, direction, subjects, and policies in China.

subfiles.title: Request for declassification of Despatch No. 19831
subfiles.about: Requests review and declassification of the 1944 London Embassy despatch transmitting the note on drug control in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Form DS-507 declassifying London Despatch No. 19831 (December 13, 1944) on drug control in Japan to unclassified, citing a June 6, 1950 memorandum.
